messages.author: f1a78b77bed56547
messages.subject: Shiny with grid engine
parts:
Hi,

Does anyone have experience using Shiny with SGE or UGE to submit batch jobs to a high performance cluster?

We  do things like using subfunctions, package, and Rcpp in the distributed processes. Because we're embedding in a Shiny app the submit overhead is also a consideration.

We've been trying snowfall with openmpi, but it's not very reliable. Rsge iseems to be defunct,  doesn't work well with package functions or Rcpp, and doesn't install with R 3.1.1. I started working on Rmpi, but it's pretty hard to use.

Before I spend a lot of time figuring out Rmpi, I wanted to ask the community if there's an approach that bubbles to the top.

Any suggestions?

Jonathan

messages.author: bbc57ffa8a14ad13
messages.subject: Re: Shiny with grid engine
parts:
I've only tinkered in this space, but my experience has been that requesting resources from SGE/UGE on-demand can often be a deal-killer for interactive Shiny apps. I've had much better luck leaving a long-running job on SGE then calling out to the resources on-demand via Rmpi (which I've found to be pretty stable, albeit without extensive testing).

I suppose the real answer is that it depends entirely on your application. I think you can have a totally reasonable use-case for on-demand SGE job submission if you hide your controls behind a submitButton to give the users the impression that their changes will all be reprocessed the moment they click that button (and the UI can respond to inform the user that the computation is ongoing and may last multiple seconds). But if you want the "true" interactive Shiny experience in which a user is able to drag a slider and immediately see their outputs update, I think submitting an SGE job is going to be a dealbreaker in that a.) there's a couple seconds of overhead to submit and return the job (at least in configurations I've worked with), and b.) the resources aren't guaranteed to be available when the job is submitted, so the user may end up waiting much longer than a few seconds.

If you have the quotas to be able to afford leaving a long-running job on SGE to support your application and interactively call out to it using Rmpi, the overhead is negligible and you know the resources are there when the app starts. It's a bit easier to manage once you've done the initial setup, and the user experience will likely be better.

My two cents. Again, without a ton of experience in this area and no code examples to share, sadly.

Good luck! Let us know what you find.

Jeff

messages.author: f1a78b77bed56547
messages.subject: Re: Shiny with grid engine
parts:
Update: I've gotten snow with Rmpi to work very well. I've since found/realized that the issue with snowfall was due to not specifying type='MPI' in sfInit(). Because I have snow working and it's  not that much more complicated than snowfall, I haven't gone back and tried snowfall with the sfInit(type='MPI') option.

Thanks for your thoughts. I really like your suggestion of opening an interactive session on Rmpi. I think for some situations that could work very well on a per session basis.

A use case would be where a user relies on interactivity to specify fairly complicated inputs to a longer running task (say from 5 seconds to 5 hours), and then interactively interrogate the results when it is done, and automate the process, so they don't have to handle submitting the jobs outside shiny. In the 5 to 60 second case we'd show a progress bar. For longer cases, we'd more likely register a job ID, and reconnect later. In either case there's still huge benefit to interactivity, and it's well understood by the user that the response time of the submit is not directly interactive.

Jonathan
